clue.text: Unwelcome extra duty

parts.note: duty reads as an added chore, but it is a tax levied by the government, and an extra one is never welcome

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about being given yet another chore.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty is a levy, so an extra one is a rise in what the Treasury takes.

clue.text: A man about a hundred will be lucky if he doesn't!

definitions.text: A man about a hundred will be lucky if he doesn't!

indicators.note: the letters for 'A man' sit around the hundred, so about signals one piece wrapping another

parts.note: he is a male person
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A centenarian is fortunate if he is spared the pains of old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts C (a hundred) inside A HE (A man). The whole clue is also the definition: a man of a hundred is lucky to be free of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A centenarian who escapes a persistent pain is fortunate indeed.

clue.text: Aid sent in alternative form

indicators.note: putting letters into another form means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Relief supplies are dispatched in a different shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges AIDSENT; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something as an alternative is doing it in place of the original.

clue.text: A high speed piece of film perhaps

definitions.meaning: to go at a fast pace is to go at a good rate
a short excerpt cut from a film or programme

explanation.surface: A fast-paced excerpt from a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Going at a fast rate is moving briskly, and a short extract from a film shares the word.

clue.text: Give exalted status to the subject?

definitions.text: Give exalted status to the subject?

parts.words: Give exalted status to the subject?
parts.note: the subject is a monarch's subject, a commoner, who is raised to the peerage

explanation.surface: Someone elevates the topic under discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a commoner into the peerage gives a title and rank.

clue.text: An irrational river in the south of France

indicators.note: the river letter sits within the French word, so in signals one piece inside another

parts.note: sud is the French word for south

explanation.surface: A mysterious waterway somewhere in Provence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the south of France' is read as the French for south, SUD, not the region; 'in' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics an irrational root, such as the square root of two, is called by this name.

clue.text: A capital picture-house

parts.note: picture-house suggests a cinema, but it is a gallery of paintings in the capital, London

explanation.surface: A fine cinema, or one in the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: This London art museum houses paintings, so it is literally a house of pictures in the capital.

clue.text: The knack of doing things dramatically

definitions.text: The knack of doing things dramatically

parts.words: The knack of doing things dramatically
parts.note: dramatically suggests flamboyant behaviour, but it means on the stage: the craft of acting

explanation.surface: Someone has a flair for making a show of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The craft of the stage actor is the skill of performing drama.

clue.text: Italy's most famous listed building

parts.note: listed suggests a protected heritage building, but here it means leaning

explanation.surface: Italy's best-known heritage-protected structure.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'listed' building in Britain is one protected for its heritage; 'list' also means lean, as a ship lists, which fits the famous leaning tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The campanile at Pisa is famous for its tilt, and to list is to lean.

clue.text: It speaks for itself as a little girl's treasured possession

definitions.text: It speaks for itself as a little girl's treasured possession

parts.words: It speaks for itself as a little girl's treasured possession
parts.note: speaks for itself is an idiom for being obvious, but here a toy literally talks

explanation.surface: A small girl's cherished toy needs no explanation.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy figure with a voice box says phrases when its string is pulled.

clue.text: Cover provided for men who go into action

definitions.text: Cover provided for men who go into action

parts.words: Cover provided for men who go into action
parts.note: cover suggests protective fire or insurance, but it is clothing issued to soldiers

explanation.surface: Protection is arranged for troops heading into combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers' field uniform is the clothing worn in combat.

clue.text: It can't help growing bitter

parts.note: reads as someone who cannot avoid becoming resentful, but it is a plant that grows with a bitter sap

explanation.surface: Someone inevitably becomes resentful.
explanation.definitionFit: This succulent plant yields a bitter juice used in medicine.

clue.text: Information obtainable from the scoreboard at a cricket match

indicators.note: the letters can be got out of the run of words that follows, so obtainable from signals a hidden word

explanation.surface: Figures can be read off the board at a cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtainable from' signals letters running across 'scoreboard at a'; 'cricket match' completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts and figures collected for reference are information.

clue.text: First lady to put on an act in Worcestershire

parts.note: in the Bible Eve is the first woman
to sham is to pretend or fake

explanation.surface: The first woman takes to the stage in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's wife but is Eve. Worcestershire is a county in the English Midlands; the answer is a market town there.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town in the Vale of that Midlands county, known for fruit growing.

clue.text: Wine that's prepared for a rainy day!

definitions.meaning: a red or white wine from Burgundy, named after its town

definitions.text: that's prepared for a rainy day!

explanation.surface: Saving a bottle for hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as MAC ON: someone with their raincoat on is ready for rain. 'For a rainy day' usually means saving for hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: A Burgundy wine takes its name from its home town; and wearing a raincoat readies you for showers.

clue.text: All-inclusive coverage for retirement

definitions.meaning: covering everything, as in a sweeping ban
retirement here is going to bed: a bed covering

explanation.surface: A pension plan that covers every eventuality.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeping rule applies everywhere; and a woollen bed covering keeps you warm when you retire for the night.

clue.text: He is a pound out on reflection

parts.note: b is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled, a way of being out

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A man admits he is a pound short when he thinks it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns L + ISA + B (pound, is a, out) back to front. In cricket scoring, b stands for bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, so 'He' stands for any man so called, as with Basil Fawlty.

clue.text: Greek princess who was showered with gold

definitions.text: Greek princess who was showered with gold

parts.words: Greek princess who was showered with gold
parts.note: in Greek myth Zeus visited an imprisoned princess as a shower of gold

explanation.surface: A mythical royal is lavished with riches.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth, the daughter of King Acrisius of Argos bore Perseus after Zeus came to her as golden rain.

clue.text: A spinner heading the averages?

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A slow bowler leads the cricket bowling averages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a spin bowler in cricket but is a spinning toy. The definition means sitting at the top of the averages.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on top of a table is sitting above all the others.

clue.text: Mrs Phillips, not Mrs Manners !

indicators.note: the clue says take away the letters of Mrs, so not signals removing them

parts.note: the letters M, R, S as written

explanation.surface: A society lady is identified as one name and not another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes M, R and S, scattered through MANNERS. Princess Anne was Mrs Mark Phillips by her first marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Princess Royal married Captain Mark Phillips in 1973.

clue.text: Strike about short work ? Get away with you !

indicators.note: the strike word goes around the short work, so about signals one piece wrapping another

parts.note: to hit is to strike
op is the short form of opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone threatens a quick blow and tells another to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' looks like the definition but is the outer piece; 'about' signals the wrap. 'Hop it' is British slang for 'go away'.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang dismissal ordering someone to leave.

clue.text: Normally the place in which Tabitha maybe found

definitions.text: Normally the place in which Tabitha maybe found

indicators.note: maybe suggests the name could be in some other order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cat called Tabitha can usually be found in her usual spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges TABITHA; the whole clue also defines a creature's natural home.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's natural home is where it normally lives.

clue.text: Dull sort of trash written about Northern Ireland

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are set around the province letters, signalling one piece wrapping another
a sort of trash is a reworked version of it, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Boring rubbish has been written about a province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges the five letters of the rubbish word into TARSH, and 'written about' wraps that around the province abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish metal is to make it lose its shine.

clue.text: Left a place to an absurdly chimerical Swiftian character

parts.note: to put is to place

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a place to a fantastical figure from Swift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word. In Swift's Gulliver's Travels, the flying island of Laputa is home to absurdly impractical theorists.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhabitant of the flying island in Gulliver's Travels, devoted to useless speculation.

clue.text: Get clean out of Arundel, maybe

indicators.note: letters taken out of their order and shaken up, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Escape cleanly from a Sussex town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' rearranges ARUNDEL, a town in Sussex; 'maybe' adds that this is one of many ways to make it.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash clothes, or illicit money, is to make it clean.

clue.text: Inactivity about the street

parts.note: re means about or concerning
ST is the standard abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Idleness is the talk of the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose is a state of doing nothing.

clue.text: She'll be a fool if she turns up!

indicators.note: in a down clue turning something up means reading it bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a nit is a fool

explanation.surface: A woman will prove herself silly if she appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses A NIT (a fool); 'if she' is filler for the surface. 'She' stands for a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, so the pronoun stands for anyone so called.

clue.text: London player manager who mastered 8 across

definitions.text: London player manager who mastered 8 across

parts.words: London player manager who mastered 8 across
parts.note: player manager sounds like football, but it means a stage actor-manager of the London theatre

explanation.surface: A London football boss who mastered the art of acting.
explanation.walkthrough: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a Victorian and Edwardian actor-manager who founded RADA and ran His Majesty's Theatre in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Beerbohm, the London actor-manager, was a master of the stage craft referred to.

clue.text: A cross that is positively significant

definitions.meaning: the mathematical addition sign is shaped as a cross
something that counts in favour, an advantage

explanation.surface: An annoyed person turns out to be a good sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The addition sign looks like an upright cross, and an advantage is a positive point.

clue.text: A stake beyond which it is intolerable to go

definitions.meaning: a pointed wooden post used in a fence

definitions.text: beyond which it is intolerable to go
definitions.meaning: from the idiom beyond the boundary of acceptable conduct

explanation.surface: A post marks the limit of what is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence post is a stake, and conduct 'beyond the pale' is outside acceptable limits.

clue.text: The pilot's last call

parts.note: last call suggests a final summons or dying words, but it is where a flight ends

explanation.surface: An airman's final words before disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A building where flights arrive is the final stop of an aircraft's journey.

clue.text: His depredations affect the stockholder

parts.note: stockholder suggests a shareholder, but it is a farmer holding livestock

explanation.surface: A fraudster's thefts hurt investors.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler steals livestock from a farmer's herd.
